subject: ACME RAG eval — recommended models, retrieval & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME RAG eval — recommended models, retrieval & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

Summary of needs
- Customer-facing knowledge base for product troubleshooting + internal KB for support agents
- Hard grounding requirement: answers must include source citations (doc id + snippet) and fall back to "I don't know" for low-confidence cases
- Latency SLO: 250–350ms p95 for single-turn retrieval + response for user-facing flows
- Throughput: 50 qps steady, occasional bursts to 200 qps
- Concern: hallucination risk on infrequent docs and potential regression if we move to smaller quantized models

Proposed evaluation approach (high level)
1) Model candidates: recommend testing llama-3-8b-ocq and redwood-14b-q4f for tradeoffs (accuracy vs cost). Also include a distilled reranker (Cross-Encoder) and a lightweight bi-encoder for recall.
2) Retrieval settings: test hybrid sparse+dense retrieval. Start with FAISS IVF-HNSW for dense with 768-d embeddings and BM25 for sparse; compare recall@1/5/10 under different chunking (500 tokens vs 1k).
3) Reranker: try a small cross-encoder reranker (re-rank top 100 -> top 5) vs a single-pass cross-encoder to measure latency/cost tradeoffs.
4) Grounding metrics: precision@1 (source cited), grounding-accuracy (manual pass on 200 queries), and EMD-style answer divergence for regression detection.
5) Prompt sets: we'll start with the prompt-set-v2.csv that Priya shared and supplement with 100 targeted edge-case queries from your support logs.

Attachments: I attached a quick benchmark plan (acme-rag-benchmarks.pdf) and the working prompt set (prompt-set-v2.csv).

Next steps
- Priya: share the support-logs sample (anonymized) and confirm the 100 edge cases by EOD Friday.
- Dev: can you propose a concrete runner config for the two model candidates + retrieval/rerank pipeline and estimated cost delta?
- Marissa: I'll schedule a short 30-min tech sync next week to kick off the eval and align success criteria.

Would Friday 11am PT for the tech sync work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa

--

We'll send over the anonymized support logs tonight.

Cheers,

Hi all —

Thanks for the detail — I sketched a concrete runner config and initial perf/cost estimates. Key points below; attaching the lightweight runner YAML and benchmarking notes inline here.

Runner config (high level) - Embeddings: Redwood-embed-1 (768d), store encrypted in your VPC (we support KMS integration for envelope encryption)
- Index: FAISS IVF-HNSW, shard size tuned for 50 qps baseline; chunking = 500 tokens (default) and test 1k tokens for comparison
- Retrieval: hybrid scoring (0.7 dense + 0.3 BM25) as a starting point; we'll sweep to find best weighting
- Reranker: two arms  a) Cross-encoder small (based on 2-3b cross-attention model) re-rank top 100->top 5 (higher accuracy, higher latency)  b) Two-stage: bi-encoder recall -> dense re-rank using lightweight mlp scorer (lower latency, lower cost)
- Generation models to test: redwood-14b-q4f, llama-3-8b-ocq, redwood-4b-8k (agent-assist)
- Fallback policy: if latency > 350ms p95 on production-like load, route to agent-assist model or degrade reranker depth to top 20

Estimated perf/cost notes (very rough)
- redwood-14b-q4f + cross-encoder rerank (top100->5): highest accuracy; expected p95 ~ 380-420ms in single-node config for user-facing path — likely needs dedicated capacity to meet 350ms
- llama-3-8b-ocq: good middle ground; p95 ~ 300-340ms; smaller cost footprint than 14b
- redwood-4b-8k (agent assist): p95 ~ 220-260ms, lowest cost, recommended for high-throughput agent flows where we can accept lower recall on corner cases

Risk & regression notes
- Quantization can introduce subtle answer divergences for rare facts; include a regression set of 200 annotated queries and diff-check answers (EMD/ROUGE + grounding-accuracy) after quantizing/compressing.
- Reranker changes can mask recall issues; track recall@1/5 and grounding-precision separately in dashboards.

Deliverables I can put together by EOD Friday:
- Runner YAML + perf/cost spreadsheet (CSV)
- Scripted evaluation harness (1000 synthetic queries + 200 manual edge cases)
- Small demo notebook showing grounding chain extraction and citation formatting

Alex — for encryption/KMS docs, see the link Marissa added; I can DM the SOC snippet if you need it for security review.

-Dev
